title: Pointwise shift compatibility of the refinement-restriction map
statement:
For every integer n and M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X)),
(((((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ push R r.hom) ⋙ pull R d.i).commShiftIso n).hom.app M ≫
  (refinementRestriction R r hi M)⟦n⟧') =
  refinementRestriction R r hi ((shiftFunctor _ n).obj M) ≫
    (((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ pull R c.i).commShiftIso n).hom.app M.

proof.text: The geometric pullback comparison is the composite of mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. Their proved shift instances in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Shift.ExactFunctor show that its hom commutes with integer shifts. Equality transport of pullback functors commutes with shifts by substituting the equality and using the identity instance. Composing these gives shift compatibility of refinementPull.

The specified proEtaleRingDerivedAdjunction is the canonical adjunction derived from the ordinary exact pullback adjunction. Apply canonicalRightDerivedAdjunctionShift and its counit instance to obtain compatibility of the proper counit with the fixed integer shifts.

For arbitrary shift-compatible K, P, L, F, G and compatible transformations epsilon : P composite L to identity and alpha : G to L composite F, assemble the natural transformation from (K composite P) composite G to K composite F using associators, whiskering alpha, whiskering epsilon, and the left unitor. Its component is alpha at P(K(M)) followed by F(epsilon at K(M)); the composition and whiskering shift instances imply its pointwise shift equation. In the geometric application first destruct the compactifications and refinement and substitute the open triangle equation, eliminating the costly equality transport. Apply this categorical calculation with K the exact derived open extension, P the proper derived pushforward, L its pullback, F the open pullback, G the target open pullback, alpha the refinement pullback comparison, and epsilon the proper counit. The component is definitionally refinementRestriction, yielding precisely the asserted equation.
